headline: State Park Camping and Mission Access
reservation: Individual campsites at Montana de Oro and Pismo State Beach require reservations six months in advance via ReserveCalifornia. The historic Mission remains an active parish; visitors should check official schedules for guided tours and liturgical closures. Regional glamping sites are high-demand and require direct booking.

days.title: Mission History and Creek Walks

stops.name: Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa
stops.detail: Tour the 1772 Spanish mission and its museum located in the heart of the historic plaza.

stops.name: Bubblegum Alley
stops.detail: Visit this quirky 70-foot long landmark covered in colorful gum for a quick local photo op.

days.driving: Walking is recommended for the downtown core; negligible drive times
days.note: Thursday nights feature a major street market; check local traffic diversions.

days.title: Volcanic Peaks and Valley Vines
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Bishop Peak Trailhead

stops.name: Bishop Peak
stops.detail: Hike the tallest of the Nine Sisters for a panoramic view of the city and the Pacific.

stops.name: Edna Valley Vineyard Region
stops.detail: Drive through the rolling hills of this cool-climate wine region south of the city.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for valley loops; conditions vary
days.note: Bishop Peak trails can be muddy and slippery following winter rains.

days.title: Rugged Cliffs and Sea Caves

stops.name: Montana de Oro State Park
stops.detail: Walk the Bluff Trail to see dramatic sea cliffs, tide pools, and crashing surf.

stops.name: Point San Luis Lighthouse
stops.detail: Access this historic site via a guided trolley or hike for views of Avila Bay.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for coastal transit; conditions vary
days.note: Access to the lighthouse is restricted; check official tour schedules for shuttle requirements.

intel.title: Downtown Structure Use
intel.text: Use the public garages on 842 Palm St or 919 Palm St for reliable downtown parking. Street meters have strict time limits and are regularly enforced.

intel.title: Coastal Microclimates
intel.text: The marine layer often persists at Montana de Oro even when downtown is sunny. Visibility on the Bluff Trail can change rapidly with incoming fog.

intel.title: Market Logistics
intel.text: The Higuera Street Farmers Market occurs every Thursday evening. Arrive before 5 PM to secure parking in the peripheral lots before street closures begin.

intel.title: Regional Range
intel.text: Ample fuel is available within city limits and along Hwy 101. Remote areas like the back of Montana de Oro have no services.

intel.title: Trailhead Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is strong in the city but weak in the deep canyons of Poly Canyon and parts of the state parks. Carry a physical map for backcountry hiking.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at SBP airport, a 10-minute drive from downtown, and check into your lodging before heading to the Mission Plaza.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are perfect for this region; no specialized off-road vehicle is required for the main sights.
plan.goldenHour: The Bluff Trail at Montana de Oro for sunset, noting the sun disappears early behind the coastal fog bank.
